(Capacity: 17,341) |champion= |tourney=[[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = Sweet Sixteen }} {{2023–24 Big East men's basketball standings}} The '''2023–24 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team''' represented [[Marquette University]] during the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by third-year head coach [[Shaka Smart]] and played their home games at [[Fiserv Forum]] in [[Milwaukee|Milwaukee, Wisconsin]] as a member of the [[Big East Conference]]. The Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team drew an average home attendance of 16,307 in 16 games in 2023-24, the 8th highest in college basketball.{{Cite web |title=Men's Basketball Attendance Records through 2024-25 |url=http://fs.ncaa.org.s3.amazonaws.com/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/Attend.pdf |website=fs.ncaa.org}} ==Previous season== The [[2022–23 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Golden Eagles]] finished the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]] 29–7, 17–3 in Big East play to win the regular season championship. They defeated [[2022–23 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]], [[2022–23 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]], and [[2022–23 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] to win the [[2023 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]]. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the East region. They defeated [[2022–23 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]] in the First Round before losing to [[2022–23 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in the Second Round of the tournament. ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- !
